name: Tweek
tagline: A minimalist weekly planner that treats your week as seven columns of checkable to-dos instead of a grid of hours.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core idea here is about forty lines of layout: seven day columns, a text input per column, drag to reorder, strike through when done. An agent will hand you a working weekly planner in one sitting and it will feel surprisingly close to the real thing, because the real thing is deliberately tiny. What you will not get in one shot is the part you actually touch every day: native mobile apps, silent sync between phone and laptop, recurring tasks that survive timezone changes, and two way calendar import. If you live in one browser on one machine, the DIY version is genuinely enough. If you plan your week on a phone in a queue, you are rebuilding a sync product, not a to-do list.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app showing a seven column week with per day task lists, add, check, drag between days, simple weekly recurrence, and arrow keys to move between weeks.
requirements: A place to run it locally, or any static host if you want it on a URL
Optional: a small VPS plus a sync endpoint if you want it on your phone too
whatYouLose: Native iOS and Android apps, which is where most of this app's usage actually happens
Invisible multi device sync with conflict handling, the genuinely hard part
Google and Apple Calendar import so scheduled events sit next to your tasks
Shared or family calendars and lightweight collaboration
Reminders and notifications that fire when you are not looking at the tab
moatNotes: The moat is restraint plus plumbing. Anyone can draw seven columns; keeping it fast, synced and boring across four platforms is the work.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because planning tools only work if they are in your pocket and always current. People pay a few dollars a month to never think about sync, to have the same week visible on a phone at a bus stop and a laptop at a desk, and to get calendar events pulled in automatically. That is infrastructure and app store presence, not features, and it is exactly what a one-shot local build skips. The DIY version wins on cost and on being yours; the paid version wins every morning you are not at your computer.
notes: One of the rare cases where the free DIY clone is aesthetically competitive on day one and operationally hopeless by week three.
prompt:
Build a minimalist weekly task planner as a local first web app in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions: Vite + React + TypeScript, plain CSS (no UI framework), Dexie for IndexedDB persistence, dnd-kit for drag and drop, date-fns for dates. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics.

Layout:
- One screen. A header with the week range (for example "Mar 3 to Mar 9"), previous week and next week buttons, and a "today" button.
- Below it, seven equal columns, Monday through Sunday, each with the weekday name and day number. Today's column gets a subtle highlight.
- Below the seven columns, one extra column-width panel called "Someday" for undated tasks.

Behavior:
- Click an empty line in a column to type a task; Enter saves and opens a new empty line under it. Escape cancels.
- Click task text to edit inline. Click the checkbox to toggle done; done tasks show strikethrough and dim, and stay in place.
- Drag tasks within a column to reorder and between columns to move days, including to and from Someday. Persist order with a float sort index.
- Support simple recurrence: a task can repeat weekly on its weekday. Store recurrence as a rule on a template record and materialize instances lazily when a week is first viewed, so editing one instance does not change the others.
- Left and right arrow keys move between weeks when no input is focused.
- Everything persists to IndexedDB immediately. No save button.

Also include:
- Export and import all data as a single JSON file, via buttons in a small settings popover.
- A dark mode toggle that follows system preference by default and is remembered.
- Keyboard reachable controls and visible focus rings.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build: login, cloud sync, mobile apps, Google or Apple Calendar integration, notifications, sharing, and any service worker beyond a basic offline cache of the built assets.

Deliver a README with install and run commands, and seed the current week with three example tasks on first launch only.
